title: Atiku Pledges Targeted Petrol Subsidy Amidst Presidential Critique
text:
Atiku Abubakar commits to reinstating a targeted petrol subsidy to ease the cost of living, while the Presidency criticises the plan as financially unsustainable and demands clarity on implementation details.
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has vowed to restore a 'targeted subsidy' on petrol if elected, pledging to make life more affordable for Nigeria ns while waiting for market forces to stabilise.
This comes as President Tinubu's administration questions the feasibility and cost of such a policy, estimating it at N19.1 trillion annually. Atiku defended his position, arguing that rising fuel prices have exacerbated poverty and that Nigeria has the wealth to provide relief to its people. The Presidency challenges Atiku to specify how this subsidy would be funded, who would benefit, and under what conditions it would be withdrawn, highlighting the political and economic tensions surrounding energy subsidies in Nigeria
